fix.shows: From the lists of names left off Uttar Pradesh's draft roll of 6 January 2026 for all 403 constituencies, the Sabar Institute counts 2,88,71,423 names, which it puts at 18.7% of the 15,44,30,092 electors on the roll before the revision, and finds 16.0% of them marked dead. It describes the other 2,42,48,090, marked permanently shifted, untraceable or absent, or already enrolled elsewhere, as alive, and says half of them are under 40. By its count 22.0% of the women and 16.5% of the men on the 2022 roll are among the names left off. The report measures these two shares against the 2022 roll because it is the latest roll split by sex, so they are shares of a different roll from the 18.7%. Outside the four city districts, among electors aged 18 to 29 marked permanently shifted, it counts 19,18,015 women and 5,37,217 men, which it reads as consistent with women moving to a husband's home after marriage. It reports that Lucknow, Ghaziabad, Gautam Buddha Nagar and Kanpur Nagar have 7.8% of the state's electors and 11.7% of the names, that Lucknow's names left off are 30.0% of its roll before the revision, and that in Allahabad North more names were left off than votes were cast in 2022. It finds that names left off for a reason other than death exceed the 2022 winning margin in 359 of the 403 seats, and names marked untraceable or absent alone in 194. It finds 1,805 of the 8,855 third gender electors on the 2022 roll, 20.4%, on the lists, and finds low turnout in 2022 the measure most closely linked to more names left off for a reason other than death. The report says the roll does not record religion, and that it estimates religion from the elector's and the relative's names with the Institute's own model. The report analyses the lists of names left off the draft roll, and Uttar Pradesh's final roll was published on 10 April 2026 with 13,39,84,792 electors. The report says that some of the people on the lists will have applied again and may appear on the final roll, and that correlation is not causation.
fix.note: First reading, 21 November 2026. The report's record read from the Institute's content API (admin.sabarinstitute.org/api/research-and-publications), since the site draws its pages in the browser, which gives it as published on 20 November 2026 at 12:26 UTC under the slug in the address above, with the title 'Uttar Pradesh SIR-2026 Draft Roll Analysis: Preliminary Report (or SIR Uttar Pradesh: Preliminary Report 2026)'. The title here is the record's second form. The report's cover reads SIR Uttar Pradesh, Preliminary Report 2026, and its PDF metadata gives the same title without the year. The report itself (SIR_Uttar_Pradesh_Preliminary_Report_SABAR.pdf, 420 pages, SHA-256 b30c65e7...0a77b, from the record's download link) read with pdftotext, the state-wide pages 1 to 16 and the conclusion on page 420 in full. The Institute announced it in a thread on X on 20 November, read from a screenshot only, because the thread could not be fetched. Its figures match the report's. The two quotes are verbatim from the executive summary on page 4. Checked against the site. Its 15,44,30,092 electors before the revision agree exactly with electors_before in data/india/states.json. Its 2,88,71,423 names are 2,644 fewer than the site's 2,88,74,067 left off the draft, from the Chief Electoral Officer's district table of 6 January 2026, and the report states that gap itself, says 52 of 75 districts match the table exactly, and says 21 of 1,77,512 polling parts have no published report. Its 16.0% marked dead agrees with the site's 16.01%. The report says the women's and men's rates use the 2022 roll, the latest split by sex, so they are shares of a different roll from the 18.7%. Allahabad North is 1,79,963 names against 1,76,058 votes in 2022 by its table. The site records Uttar Pradesh's final roll as published on 10 April 2026, before the report, and the report does not compare its lists with that roll. Every figure the report gives by religion, from its name-reading model, and its tables of caste and of the last words in names are not carried. The report's comparison of the seats won by the two alliances in 2022 is not carried, because it frames the names left off by party. The report's account of the effect of deletions on services in West Bengal, and its call for a countrywide study, are its own and are not carried.
